messages:
mira: Quick heads-up — I ran the long-context KV stress harness on argo-14b-q8 (int8 deriv) with interleaved-prefix priming. Seeing consistent divergence in generated token stream right after a prefix eviction at ~23.5k tokens.

kevin: Ugh. Did you run with the new RoPE multiplier change from yesterday?

mira: Yep — prod-rope-scaling=v2 (the fractional rescale fix). Reproduced with and without the rescale patch; divergence is much less frequent without interleaving, but still present occasionally.

sylvia: Can you paste the minimal repro command and a tiny trace? :eyes:

mira: Command I used:
```
./bench/longctx_kvcache.py --model argo-14b-q8 --quant int8 --run-length 50000 --prefill-mode interleaved --rope-mode fractional-v2 --seed 42
```
Short trace excerpt (token indices):
```
[23280] prefix-evict -> kv-window shrank to 24576
[23301] generated token "the"
[23302] generated token "company"
[23303] generated token "of"  <-- expected punctuation
[23304] generated token "company"  <-- repeat (divergence starts)
```
Full artifacts: s3://redwood-ml/bench/1732123456/argo-14b-q8/trace.tsv

zane: quant-bench-bot summary?

quant-bench-bot: Run complete. Quality delta: -1.7% (argmax BLEU-like proxy) at 23,500–24,200 tokens. Latency stable. Artifacts uploaded. /cc @mira @kevin

anya: Do we think this is a KV-index aliasing bug or RoPE wrap/mismatch during eviction?

mira: My current hypothesis: when interleaved prefill writes fragments across the rolling shard boundary, the fractional RoPE rescale + int8 packing yields a small phase offset that under eviction becomes amplified — leads to token drift. Non-interleaved prefill reduces the chance because data is contiguous in the KV buffer.

kevin: Good hypothesis. Steps to triage: 1) deterministic prefill (no interleave) 2) force full-copy on eviction (avoid compacting) 3) run with int4 fallback to see quant sensitivity 4) generate kernel-level dumps to check rotary phase vectors across shards.

sylvia: I can set up (1) and (2) now. Which config flags?

mira: For (1): --prefill-mode contiguous. For (2): set env PREFILL_EVICT_STRATEGY=copy-full. For kernel dumps add --dump-kv-phase=/tmp/phase-dumps and zip to S3.

zane: I'll spin up an int4 matrix run later tonight (nightly cluster) and add the exact diff for the quant packer.

kevin: Also add a short test that injects a tiny phase perturbation on prefill to see sensitivity curve. If small perturb becomes >0.5 token shift after eviction that's a smoking gun.

anya: If it is amplification from rescale, fallback could be to temporarily disable fractional rescale for evicted fragments or force re-normalize on merge. But need to measure perf hit.

mira: Agreed. I'll run (1)+(2) now and post quick logs. Current plan: run 3x seeds for each config and collect the token-alignment diff metric and the per-layer RoPE phase L2 across shards.

quant-bench-bot: Quick note: scheduled int4 run on night cluster (job 7731) — will report delta and upload artifacts to s3://redwood-ml/bench/1732123456/argo-14b-q8/int4/ when done.

mira: Posting first 10k lines from the phase dump (trimmed):
```
layer3: shard0 mean-phase=0.0032 mean-delta=0.00012
layer3: shard1 mean-phase=0.0034 mean-delta=0.00087  <-- jump after eviction
layer12: shard3 mean-phase=0.0012 mean-delta=0.00009
```
Pattern looks localized to mid layers.

kevin: Mid layers being sensitive makes sense — that's where attention keys dominate semantics. Good call on targeted kernel dumps.

sylvia: Running contiguous+copy-full now (job 7728). ETA ~12m. I'll paste pass/fail.

mira: Thanks. If contiguous eliminates the divergence, that's pretty strong evidence for interleaved write ordering + rescale being the culprit. If not, next is to bisect the eviction compact routine.

anya: Also maybe run a short A/B where we disable the rescale but keep interleaving; that'll show whether rescale is necessary for amplification.

mira: Will do that after 7728. Thanks team. I'll update this thread with S3 links and a short write-up next. :thumbsup:
